fabric-api-base.reason: Shipped by Fabricated (vendored from upstream); every Fabric API module builds on it.

fabric-api-lookup-api-v1.reason: Shipped by Fabricated (unchanged from upstream) because its transfer API builds on it.

fabric-block-api-v1.reason: Shipped by Fabricated on NeoForge's block hooks (upstream's mixins conflict with NeoForge's patches); NeoForge's own chunk-section air check is kept.

fabric-client-gametest-api-v1.reason: development-time test framework, not needed to play

fabric-content-registries-v0.reason: Shipped by Fabricated: upstream's registries and mixins, with NeoForge's data maps backed by them where an entry is missing.

fabric-crash-report-info-v1.reason: NeoForge already lists every mod in crash reports; nothing else to provide.

fabric-data-generation-api-v1.reason: development-time data generator, not needed to play

fabric-dimensions-v1.reason: DataFixerUpper is a library NeoForge loads without mixin support, so the safety net for worlds that reference a removed modded dimension is not available.

fabric-entity-events-v1.reason: Shipped by Fabricated on NeoForge's entity events (upstream's mixins conflict with NeoForge's patches); elytra and most sleep events are not fired.

fabric-events-interaction-v0.reason: Shipped by Fabricated on NeoForge's interaction events (upstream's mixins conflict with NeoForge's patches); attack entity callbacks get no hit result, and client-side cancelled interactions still reach the server.

fabric-game-rule-api-v1.reason: /gamerule does not list Fabric's custom rule types on 1.21.11 (the mixin targets a synthetic field NeoForge's build does not have); the rules themselves work.

fabric-gametest-api-v1.reason: development-time test framework, not needed to play

fabric-item-api-v1.reason: Shipped by Fabricated on NeoForge's item hooks and events (upstream's mixins conflict with NeoForge's patches); equipment slot providers get no entity, tooltip appenders are added after the other tooltip lines.

fabric-lifecycle-events-v1.reason: Shipped by Fabricated on NeoForge's events (upstream's mixins conflict with NeoForge's patches).

fabric-loot-api-v3.reason: Shipped by Fabricated: upstream's builder and drop mixins as they are, its loading hook replaced by NeoForge's LootTableLoadEvent (upstream's conflicts with NeoForge's loot loading).

fabric-model-loading-api-v1.reason: Model loading plugins, extra models (added to the models NeoForge's own overload of the discovery resolves) and model modifiers work. Fabric's custom model formats (fabric:type in model and blockstate files) work through NeoForge's parsers, next to NeoForge's own (loader, type): upstream's hooks into vanilla's parsers are left out, because NeoForge's model file deserializer takes precedence over upstream's and upstream's blockstate codec would replace NeoForge's. It loads without the renderer API, which only its wrapper and composite models' emitQuads use; NeoForge never calls those.

fabric-networking-api-v1.reason: Shipped by Fabricated on NeoForge's payload system (login queries are not supported).

fabric-object-builder-api-v1.reason: Shipped by Fabricated on NeoForge's registration events (upstream's mixins conflict with NeoForge's patches); custom minecart comparator logic is not used by detector rails; trades are replayed through NeoForge's trade events.

fabric-particles-v1.reason: NeoForge builds sprint and fall particles with their block position already; upstream's mixins add it to the vanilla constructor NeoForge no longer calls. On 1.21.11 NeoForge decides whether block breaking particles are tinted (IClientBlockExtensions.areBreakingParticlesTinted), so ParticleRenderEvents.ALLOW_BLOCK_DUST_TINT does not fire.

fabric-recipe-api-v1.reason: NeoForge already gives Ingredient a hashCode, which upstream's mixin would replace.

fabric-registry-sync-v0.reason: Shipped by Fabricated on NeoForge's registries, which already sync ids to clients (upstream's mixins conflict with NeoForge's patches).

fabric-renderer-api-v1.reason: Fabric's renderer API replaces the block model pipeline that NeoForge owns; mods that require it need their NeoForge build.

fabric-renderer-indigo.reason: Fabric's renderer API replaces the block model pipeline that NeoForge owns; mods that require it need their NeoForge build.

fabric-rendering-fluids-v1.reason: NeoForge tints fluids through their fluid type and decides where they show their overlay texture with BlockState.shouldDisplayFluidOverlay, instead of the code upstream modifies: Fabricated applies a Fabric fluid render handler's color to NeoForge's tint, and blocks marked transparent through FluidRenderingRegistry.setBlockTransparency keep NeoForge's behavior. Custom fluid renderers and sprites work.

fabric-rendering-v1.reason: NeoForge draws the HUD in layers: Fabricated runs Fabric's HUD elements from NeoForge's vanilla layers and fires HudRenderCallback after them instead of upstream's HUD mixin. NeoForge keeps block colors in a map by block: Fabricated looks colors up there instead of upstream's method. Picture-in-picture renderers registered with Fabric are not used (NeoForge rebuilt that renderer), the debug options screen keeps vanilla's sorting and search, and render pipeline snippets don't carry Fabric's GUI draw mode flag (NeoForge added a field to them); pipelines do.

fabric-resource-conditions-api-v1.reason: NeoForge decides whether data files and registry entries load with its own conditions: Fabricated evaluates fabric:load_conditions there, with upstream's conditions, instead of upstream's mixins on the code NeoForge rewrote.

fabric-resource-loader-v1.reason: Shipped by Fabricated on NeoForge's reload-listener and pack-finder events (upstream's mixins conflict with NeoForge's patches).

fabric-screen-api-v1.reason: NeoForge draws screens through its own hook: Fabricated fires the before/after render events from NeoForge's screen render events instead of upstream's wrapper.

fabric-screen-handler-api-v1.reason: Shipped by Fabricated on NeoForge's menu opening data: extended menus send their opening data the way NeoForge mods' menus do (upstream's mixins target the openMenu NeoForge replaced).

fabric-sound-api-v1.reason: NeoForge asks each sound instance for its audio stream: Fabricated uses a Fabric sound instance's own stream there instead of upstream's redirect.

fabric-tag-api-v1.reason: NeoForge tag files already have a remove list, which NeoForge applies: Fabricated adds fabric:remove entries to it instead of upstream's own removal handling.

fabric-transfer-api-v1.reason: Shipped by Fabricated: upstream's API and mixins, with the container mixins reworked onto NeoForge's transaction-aware setItem; NeoForge hoppers don't see Fabric-only storages yet.
